## EMST role: Wildlife biologist (state variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.5, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R15-wildlife-biologist/state:2683`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — journey L2
- Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys — journey L2
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — journey L2
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — journey L2
- Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions — journey L2
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — journey L2
- Adjudicate automated species detections using field-formed identification expertise — journey L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — journey L2
- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — journey L2
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — journey L2
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits
- Apply zoonotic disease and personal safety precautions when handling wildlife, including protective equipment and decontamination
- Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata
- Conduct ground or aerial counts of target species along defined survey units to support abundance estimation
- Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern
- Observe animal movement, foraging and breeding behaviour at study sites, recording behaviour and habitat context on standardized forms
- Identify regional plants and animals to species with dichotomous keys and diagnostic features, collecting evidence for any record not identified with certainty
- Verify species records submitted by crews or volunteers against attached photos, recordings or vouchers before they enter the program database

## EMST role: Fisheries and aquatic biologist (state variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.55, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R16-fisheries-aquatic-biologist/state:2683`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Manage fish populations and habitats to stated conservation and harvest objectives — journey L2
- Conduct fisheries stock assessments and develop management advice — journey L2
- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — journey L2
- Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings — journey L2
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — journey L2
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — journey L2
- Operate fish hatchery and aquatic propagation programmes — journey L2
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — journey L2
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — journey L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — journey L2
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Sample fish populations by electrofishing, netting or hydroacoustics following the survey protocol to estimate abundance and size structure
- Assess water quality and habitat conditions limiting a fish population, identifying the factors management can change
- Estimate age, growth and mortality of a fish population from scale or otolith readings and catch-curve data
- Fit a stock assessment model to catch, survey and biological data, documenting model diagnostics and retrospective patterns
- Apply a data-limited assessment method to a stock with sparse catch and survey data, stating the uncertainty in reference points
- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits
- Execute person-overboard, capsize and cold-water immersion procedures for a small-boat crew during drills and real events
- Work sampling gear such as grabs, nets, sondes or traps over the side of a small vessel, keeping crew clear of lines and winches
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection
- Screen field measurement results against applicable water-quality criteria before leaving the site, triggering resampling or notification when an exceedance appears
